atoms.text: The Stonewall Riots, or simply Stonewall, began on June 28, 1969 in New York City and marked the beginning of the gay rights movement in the United States and around the world. The pride parade is celebrated every year because of Stonewall, and is a celebration of and protest for gay rights. Some important organisers at the time were Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera.

Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera were transgender activists who fought for gay rights and organised to protect homeless gay youth. The Stonewall Inn was a gay bar on Christopher Street in Greenwich Village in New York City. In the 1960s same-sex relations were illegal, in other words, it was illegal to be gay. People could be sent to jail for being openly gay in public, so at the time, many people found connections in gay bars and clubs. The majority of these bars and clubs were owned and run by the mafia who would pay off the police, so the police would not bother the people inside the bar.

However, on the 28th June 1969, the police came into the Stonewall Inn and began arresting and beating the people inside. On that night something changed and the gay community decided it had had enough, and began to fight back. The very first pride parade was on the one-year anniversary of the Stonewall Riots and continues today, typically on the same day every year. Although it took a long time for gay people to have their rights respected, and discrimination still happens today, the Stonewall Riots, Marsha P. Johnson, Sylvia Rivera and other activists changed the world forever.
